data.name: Gentilis
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'gentilis', meaning 'born in a family' or 'kind'. This name was given to those who were not Roman citizens, but were kind and hospitable to Romans. It is a reminder of the importance of being welcoming and gracious to all people.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embrace hospitality and kindness, opening your heart to all.

data.cultural_impact: The term 'Gentile' has been used both historically and culturally to refer to those outside of a particular group or community. In the context of Christianity, it underscores the importance of welcoming those who are different and embracing them as part of the larger spiritual family. It serves as a reminder that diversity is a strength and that love and inclusion should be at the heart of all communities.
data.spiritual_significance: The name 'Gentilis' carries with it a deep spiritual significance. It is a reminder that God's love is not limited to any particular race, nationality, or background. The name invites us to be inclusive, loving, and gracious to all people, regardless of their differences. As Christians, we are called to follow in the footsteps of Jesus and to extend God's love to all, just as the Gentiles were welcomed into the early Christian community. By embracing the name 'Gentilis', we are reminded of the importance of welcoming the stranger, extending kindness to those who may be different, and building a spiritual community grounded in love and unity.
